rationale: This is a very small C++ program (245 lines, ~4.4 KB text, 26 functions) with class-based virtual dispatch (rectangle::draw, line::draw, myshape ctor), so the budget is dominated by size and marginal-return reasoning. SUB is cheap and safe, so it gets low cost weights and is enabled broadly as the baseline layer. FLA is prioritized on the few meaningful functions (main at 1017 bytes, rectangle::draw at 811) where flattening actually obscures structure, but its RuntimeCost weight (0.7) is kept high so it is not applied indiscriminately to trivial getters; SPLIT is weighted as a cheap enabler that increases FLA/BCF efficacy on these larger functions. BCF gets strong security weight but an elevated SizeCost (0.7) because bogus blocks and opaque predicates bloat a binary this small quickly. IBR and ICALL are moderately favored since C++ vtable dispatch already normalizes indirect control flow, limiting their marginal diversity gain, and their higher CorrectnessRisk weights (0.4) protect exception tables, vtable references, and relocation-sensitive sites in this C++ codebase. IGV rounds out data-side resistance against class/vtable recovery with moderate weights across the board, keeping overall overhead acceptable for a program whose functions are mostly tiny.
